### Access

*function* · tier: stable · `import { Access } from "@afora/core"`

Says who may call a use case, on the class itself:

```ts

### AccessDeclaration

*type* · tier: stable · `import type { AccessDeclaration } from "@afora/core"`

Who may call a use case, as data: declared with the `access` setting of
`useCaseOf` or with `@Access`, and enforced by every output before the use
case runs. `{ public: true }` lets anyone in. Any other declaration needs
an authenticated caller (`{}` asks for nothing more), and may add:

- `scopes`: the caller has all of them;
- `owner`: the input key `input` equals the subject of the caller, or its
  claim `claim`;
- `context`: keys of the context of the call filled from the caller, over
  whatever the request sent.

### IBlueprint

*interface* · tier: stable · `import type { IBlueprint } from "@afora/core"`

A blueprint: an object shape of named fields, made by {@link blueprintOf }. It
parses a value with `safeParse` or its Standard Schema (`~standard`), joins

record (see {@link recordOf }). `Optional` is `true` for one that, as a field,

### applicationOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { applicationOf } from "@afora/core"`

A named, immutable manifest of what an application declares, so that all of
it runs in one place and can be introspected, e.g.
`applicationOf({ name: "blog", entities: { User, Post }, repositories: { Users, Posts } })`.

Each collection is `{ Name: declaration }`. At declaration it checks the set
as a whole: the same object under two names, an entity or record held (at
any depth) by a registered blueprint, record, entity or repository that is
not registered, and a repository whose entity, relations or environments
are not. `extends` inherits the declarations of other applications: the
same object under the same name is registered once, and different objects
under one name (or one object under two names) throw `ApplicationConflict`.
`describe()` gives the graph. With a `provider` (or that of the last
application extended that has one), `repositories` are bound to it.

**Throws** {

**Throws** {

**Throws** {

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import {
	applicationOf,
	blueprintOf,
	entityOf,
	inMemoryProvider,
	repositoryOf,
} from "@afora/core";

class User extends entityOf(blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ name: ctx.string }))) {}
const Users = repositoryOf({ entity: User, actions: ["create"] });

const Blog = applicationOf({
	name: "blog",
	entities: { User },
	repositories: { Users },
	provider: inMemoryProvider(), // the default of its repositories
});

await Blog.start();
await Blog.repositories.Users.create({ name: "Ana" });
await Blog.stop();
```

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf } from "@afora/core";

const Signup = blueprintOf((ctx) => ({
	name: ctx.text,
	email: ctx.email, // trimmed and lowercased
	tags: ctx.listOf(ctx.string, { maxItems: 5 }),
	nickname: ctx.optional.string,
}));

const parsed = Signup.safeParse({
	name: "Ana",
	email: " ANA@example.com ",
	tags: [],
});
if (!parsed.issues) parsed.value.email; // "ana@example.com"
```

`recordPluginCatalogOf`.

### entityOf

*const* · tier: stable · `import { entityOf } from "@afora/core"`

An entity of `blueprint`: a record with an `id` (a UUID v7, in
`options.unique`) and a `createdAt`, both made when missing from its value,
an `updatedAt` set by each change, and a `deletedAt` set by `destroy`, after
which it no longer changes; with `expires: { after }`, an `expiresAt` too.
E.g.
`class User extends entityOf(blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ name: ctx.string }))) {}`.
As a record, the class can be a field of another blueprint, e.g.
`{ author: User }`, with `optionalOf` and `listOf`. `options.plugins` picks
from the standard plugins, as `(ctx) => [ctx.publishable]`, or takes any
plugin made by {@link recordPluginOf }.

**Throws** {

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf, entityOf } from "@afora/core";

class User extends entityOf(
	blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ name: ctx.string })),
	{ change: ["name"] },
) {}

const user = new User({ name: "Jane" });
user.id; // a UUID v7
user.updatedAt; // undefined until the first change
user.change.name("Ann").updatedAt; // now
user.destroy().isDeleted; // true
```

### environmentOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { environmentOf } from "@afora/core"`

The environment `blueprint` describes: `load` reads the declared variables
from `options.source` (`process.env` by default), converts each to a
boolean (`"true"`, `"false"`) or a number when its property takes one
instead of a string, validates them once and
gives the same value after. As a dependency of a repository it reaches the
provider as `context.env`; of a use case ({@link useCaseOf }), the use case gets its value, e.g.
`environmentOf(blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ DATABASE_URL: ctx.url })))`.

**Throws** {TypeError} when `blueprint` is not a blueprint, or is an optional one.

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf, environmentOf } from "@afora/core";

const Env = environmentOf(
	blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ DATABASE_URL: ctx.url, PORT: ctx.integer })),
	{ source: () => ({ DATABASE_URL: "https://db.example.com", PORT: "3000" }) },
);

Env.load().PORT; // 3000, converted from the string
// Env.load() throws InvalidEnvironment when a variable is missing or invalid
```

### eventOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { eventOf } from "@afora/core"`

Defines an event without executing its handler. Without a handler, the
event only carries the entity, for a policy such as `publishEvents`, and
`handle()` does nothing.

**Throws** {TypeError} when `entityClass` is not an entity class, or `handler` is given and is not a function.

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf, type EventDefinition, entityOf, eventOf } from "@afora/core";

class Post extends entityOf(blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ title: ctx.string }))) {
	publish(): void {
		this.emit(PostPublished);
	}
}

// The annotation breaks TypeScript's circular inference through the base class.
const PostPublished: EventDefinition = eventOf(
	"post.published",
	Post,
	async (post, { logger }) => logger.info("post.published", { id: post.id }),
);

const post = new Post({ title: "Hi" });
post.publish();
for (const event of post.pullEvents()) await event.handle();
```

### eventPolicyOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { eventPolicyOf } from "@afora/core"`

A factory of event policies for the `events` setting of `commandOf`:
`events: publishEvents({ publisher: "realtime", topic: "posts/{id}" })`.
Its options are JSON, checked by `validate` when the policy is made (an
`InvalidEventPolicy` otherwise), so the policy can be written in an
`afora.json` and an application describes it by name and options instead
of `{ kind: "opaque" }`. `handle` gets the events of a call that succeeded,
what a handler policy gets, and the options.

### exceptionOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { exceptionOf } from "@afora/core"`

Declares an exception of `layer`, e.g.
`throw new PropertyRequired({ source: "email" })`. Its `details` are typed
by the parameter of `message`, when it is a function.

**Example**

```ts
import { ExceptionLayers, exceptionOf } from "@afora/core";

const UserNotFound = exceptionOf({
	layer: ExceptionLayers.UseCase,
	name: "UserNotFound",
	message: ({ id }: { id: string }) => `There is no user ${id}.`,
});

const error = new UserNotFound({ source: "FindUser", details: { id: "42" } });
error.message; // "There is no user 42."
error.layer; // ExceptionLayers.UseCase
```

### guard

*function* · tier: stable · `import { guard } from "@afora/core"`

Handles what `run` throws, or rejects with, in `scope` (see {@link ExceptionScope}). Without `resolve`,
or when it calls `pass`, the exception goes up to the next layer with its
trace; otherwise `resolve` returns the value to use instead.

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import { ExceptionLayers, guard } from "@afora/core";

const scope = { layer: ExceptionLayers.UseCase, source: "LoadConfig" };

// Without `resolve`, what `run` throws goes up to the next layer with its trace
guard(scope, () => JSON.parse('{"port":3000}'));

// With `resolve`, it can give a value instead, or call `pass` to go up
const config = guard(
	scope,
	() => JSON.parse("{") as { port: number },
	() => ({ port: 8080 }),
);
```

### inMemoryProvider

*function* · tier: stable · `import { inMemoryProvider } from "@afora/core"`

A provider that keeps the values in memory, one table per entity name it
declares (or per entity class, without one), enforcing its unique keys. Each `repositoryOf` without a provider gets its
own; repositories given the same one share the tables of their entities.
Its `transaction` works on isolated snapshots: commits on success, discards
on rejection, runs one at a time and makes other operations wait; nested
transactions are savepoints.

### openapi

*const* · tier: stable · `import { openapi } from "@afora/core"`

Builds an OpenAPI 3.1 document from the operations.

Routes: `POST {basePath}/{kebab(command)}/{kebab(operation)}`, changed per
operation id with `route`; two operations on one method and path throw
`InvalidOutputStage`. A `{name}` segment of a path is a required path
parameter, the input key `name` (a scalar), left out of the body or query.
The `operationId` is the id with its dot as an underscore (`Users.register`
-> `Users_register`), unique or the build throws. `get` and `delete` send
the input as query parameters, which needs every input field to be a
scalar property. Responses: the `route` status (`200` by default; `204`
without content) with the response schema and the `responses` headers,
`400` and `500` always, and the status of each declared error (`statusOf`:
`statuses` of the output, else 422); `requestId` adds its header to all of
them. Operations carry no repository dependencies, so `404` and `409`
appear only when an error that maps to them is declared. Records and
entities reachable from inputs and responses are named by class name in
`components.schemas`, beside `Problem` (RFC 9457). `security` gives
`components.securitySchemes`, the document `security` (`default`) and the
`security` of each operation. The `context` of an operation is
transport-specific and not part of the document; sinks that serve HTTP map
it (headers, middleware).

*function* · tier: stable · `import { operationOf } from "@afora/core"`

A modified copy of `operation`. Only `meta` (replaced), `tags`,
`description`, `deprecated` and `invoke` can change; `kind`, `version`,
`id`, `command`, `name`, `useCase`, `input`, `response`, `context` and
`errors` cannot, and a patch naming them throws `InvalidOutputStage`.

The version of `Property` that accepts `undefined`. Returns `Property` itself
when it is already optional, and the same class for the same `Property`.
The version of `blueprint` that, as a field of another blueprint, accepts
`undefined`. Returns `blueprint` itself when it is already optional.
The version of `list` that, as a field of a blueprint, accepts `undefined`.
The version of `variant` that, as a field of a blueprint, accepts `undefined`.
The version of `record` that, as a field of a blueprint, accepts `undefined`
or an instance of `record`. Returns `record` itself when it is already optional.
The version of any blueprint field that accepts `undefined`.

An output turns commands into operations and runs them through a pipe of

What `field` declares under `PropertyInput`; `undefined` for a property

property.

### propertyOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { propertyOf } from "@afora/core"`

Declares a property: a class that holds one value, run through
`preHandle`, the validation against the TypeBox `schema` and
`afterHandle`. `optional`, `sensitive` and `unique` flag it for the
blueprints and records that hold it, and `default` is its `demo()` value.
Extend the class to add behavior, or narrow it with `.with(options)`. A
value its schema rejects makes the constructor throw
{@link InvalidPropertyValue }, and `undefined` for a required one
{@link PropertyRequired }.

**Example**

```ts
import { propertyOf } from "@afora/core";
import { Type } from "typebox";

const Name = propertyOf({
	name: "name",
	schema: Type.String({ minLength: 3 }),
	preHandle: (value) => value.trim(),
	default: "Jane", // used by Name.demo()
});

new Name("  Alice ").value; // "Alice"
Name.demo().value; // "Jane"
// new Name("a") throws InvalidPropertyValue
```

### providerFrom

*function* · tier: stable · `import { providerFrom } from "@afora/core"`

A provider made on `app.start()`: `create` gets the variables of
`environmentDependencies` (one environment or a list, merged in order),
read and validated then, e.g.
`providerFrom(Database, (env) => drizzleProvider({ db: connect(env.DATABASE_URL), tables }))`.
A provider made on `app.start()` from the context of the application:
`ctx.env(Database)` gives the variables of a registered environment and
`ctx.logger` its logger, e.g.
`providerFrom((ctx) => drizzleProvider({ db: connect(ctx.env(Database).DATABASE_URL), tables }))`.

### providersOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { providersOf } from "@afora/core"`

Named providers, declared once in a module of their own so that
repositories can name one before any application exists, e.g.
`const Providers = providersOf({ main: providerFrom(Database, ...), audit: auditProvider() })`,
then `repositoryOf({ ..., provider: Providers.audit })` and
`applicationOf({ providers: Providers, provider: Providers.main, ... })`.
Each value is a provider or a factory of `providerFrom`; an application
that registers the storage makes each factory on `start()`, its own
instance (an application that extends it shares them).

### publishEvents

*const* · tier: stable · `import { publishEvents } from "@afora/core"`

An event policy that publishes the events of a call to a publisher of the
application, once the call succeeded (and committed):
`events: publishEvents({ publisher: "realtime", topic: "posts/{id}" })`.

For each event, in order, it runs the event's own handler first (unless
`handle: false`), then publishes `{ name, command, operation, entity }`
to the topic, the entity as JSON with sensitive values masked; the context
and the variables are never published. `events` limits it to some names.
A handler that fails stops the call with `CommandEventFailed`, as with
`"after-commit"`. A publish that fails is logged and skipped
(`onPublishError: "log"`, the default) or fails the call (`"throw"`). A
publisher the application does not declare fails the call, caused by
`PublisherNotBound`.

a later catalog replaces a plugin of an earlier one with the same name.

class Account extends recordOf(

*function* · tier: stable · `import { recordPluginCatalogOf } from "@afora/core"`

A catalog of `plugins`, by name: what `recordBuilderOf` and
`entityBuilderOf` give `options.plugins` to pick from, as

### recordPluginOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { recordPluginOf } from "@afora/core"`

A plugin of the record class `Record`, named `name`: the records and
entities that declare it in `options.plugins` get the keys of its
blueprint, its sensitive, unique and `change` keys, the methods and getters
its class declares, and its `onSet` and `onSetAll` effects, which run for
changes to its keys; the plugins of `Record` are applied with it. The
constructor of `Record` does not run for them, and its methods cannot use
private (`#`) members. E.g.
`recordPluginOf("publishable", Publishable, { version: "1.0.0" })`.

### repositoryOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { repositoryOf } from "@afora/core"`

A repository of `entity` with the methods of `actions`: `findBy<Key>` for a
unique key (`id`, `options.unique`, a `unique` property), giving the entity
or `undefined`; `findManyBy<Key>` for any other key, giving a list;
`create`, `update`, `delete`, `restore` (soft deletion only), `increment`, `count`, and the queries `findMany`,
`exists`, `findPage` and `findCursor`, and `forEachPage`, which walks the
pages of a cursor query, resumably. Every method is async and reads and writes through `provider`
(a new {@link inMemoryProvider } by default), which gets the variables of
`environmentDependencies` as `context.env`. The repository can be a
dependency of a use case, and {@link RepositoryOf} extends it with a class.

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf, entityOf, repositoryOf } from "@afora/core";

class User extends entityOf(
	blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ name: ctx.string, email: ctx.email })),
	{ unique: ["email"] },
) {}

const Users = repositoryOf({
	entity: User,
	actions: ["findByEmail", "create"],
});

await Users.create({ name: "Ana", email: "ana@example.com" });
const ana = await Users.findByEmail("ana@example.com"); // User | undefined
```

### resourceOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { resourceOf } from "@afora/core"`

The use cases of a CRUD resource over `repository`, for the `useCases` of
`commandOf`: the standard `create`, `get`, `list`, `update` and `delete`,
each with the route of a REST resource at `path`.

```ts
const Blog = commandOf({
	name: "Blog",
	useCases: resourceOf(Posts, { path: "/posts" }),
});
// POST /posts (201), GET /posts, GET /posts/{id}, PATCH /posts/{id}, DELETE /posts/{id}
```

It is only a shortcut for
`(ctx) => ({ create: ctx.create(Posts, { route }), ... })`: the command it
goes into is an ordinary one, and `describe()` shows the same standard use
cases. `actions` picks some of the operations, and `access` says who may
call them. A repository that lacks the action of an operation throws
`UseCaseUnavailable` when the command is declared. For anything else an
operation needs (`omit`, `owner`, hooks), write that one with `ctx` and
spread the rest: `(ctx) => ({ ...resourceOf(Posts, options)(ctx), create: ctx.create(Posts, { ... }) })`.

### stripUndeclared

*function* · tier: stable · `import { stripUndeclared } from "@afora/core"`

A copy of `value` without the keys `shape` does not declare, at any depth:
in nested blueprints, the items of `listOf`, `optionalOf` and the records
and entities held as fields. For a payload with more than the operation
reads, such as a webhook from another service, before it is parsed, since
parsing rejects an undeclared key (`undeclared_key`).

It does not validate, never throws and does not change `value`: a value of
the wrong type, a property's value (even an object) and a record instance
come back as they are, for parsing to accept or reject.

### toOpenAPI

*function* · tier: stable · `import { toOpenAPI } from "@afora/core"`

The OpenAPI 3.1 schema (a JSON Schema) of a property, blueprint, list,
record or entity, every nested record inline. Each `description`,
`examples`... given with `Property.with` is kept; sensitive keys are
`writeOnly`, the identity of an entity (`id`, `createdAt`, ...) `readOnly`,
optional keys left out of `required`, and objects closed with
`additionalProperties: false`.
The `components` of an OpenAPI document for `models`, by name, e.g.
`toOpenAPI({ User, Post })`: a record named among them is a `$ref` wherever
another model holds it, as `{ $ref: "#/components/schemas/User" }`.

### useCaseOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { useCaseOf } from "@afora/core"`

Declares an operation. With `steps` the class is concrete: its `execute`
interprets them. Without, it is abstract: extend it and implement an async
execute method.

**Throws** {

**Example**

```ts
import { blueprintOf, useCaseOf } from "@afora/core";

class Greet extends useCaseOf({
	name: "Greet",
	blueprint: blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ name: ctx.text })),
	response: blueprintOf((ctx) => ({ message: ctx.string })),
}) {
	override async execute() {
		return { message: `Hello, ${this.input.name}!` };
	}
}

const { message } = await new Greet({ name: "Ana" }).execute();
```

### useCasePluginOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { useCasePluginOf } from "@afora/core"`

A use case that is made for a repository. `settings.compile` gets what is
known of the repository and its entity (`UseCaseTargetInfo`) and the
options of the call, and gives the settings of `useCaseOf` with `steps`;
`settings.requires` lists the actions and record plugins it cannot do
without. The plugin's `make(repository, options)` gives the class, the
same for the same repository and equal options.

`Make` types that call: give it to say which repositories are accepted
(`UseCaseTarget`) and what the use case takes and returns. Without it any
repository is accepted and the class is `AnyUseCaseClass`.

Throws `InvalidUseCasePlugin` for a name that is not an identifier, a
version that is not semantic or a `compile` that is not a function.

### variantOf

*function* · tier: stable · `import { variantOf } from "@afora/core"`

A field holding one of several objects, told apart by the value of `key`:
`variantOf("type", { click: Click, signup: Signup })` takes
`{ type: "click", ...a Click }` or `{ type: "signup", ...a Signup }`. Each
variant is a blueprint, which does not declare `key`: the field adds it,
with the name of the variant for its value. A variant can also be a record
class (an entity too): the value is then an instance of it, told apart by
its class, and the key is only in what is given, in `toJSON` and in what is
stored.

### compileRoutes

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { compileRoutes } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The routes of `operations`, compiled once, for a sink that serves HTTP on
any server: the sink routes each `method` and `path` to `handle` and sends
the result as is. Everything a request needs is decided here, so a call
only reads, coerces and runs:

- The input is the JSON body of a `post`, `put` or `patch` and the query
  of a `get` or `delete`, with the keys the route reads elsewhere over it:
  `{name}` segments of the path, and the query keys, headers and cookies
  the use case route declares. Text is coerced to the numbers and booleans
  the input takes; the operation validates it (a 400 problem with `issues`).
- The context comes from `context.headers` (coerced) and
  `context.variables` (as is); a missing one leaves the key out.
- An operation with an `access` other than `public` asks
  `settings.authenticator` who calls; without one, or without credentials,
  it is a 401.
- Success is the route status with the response as JSON (sensitive values
  masked by `toJSON`), or no body for `204`, plus the `responses` headers.
  Errors are `application/problem+json`, with the status of `statusOf`
  (the output `statuses` first). `requestId` puts the request id on every
  result, `notFound` and `failure` included.
- `docs.path` serves the `openapi` document of the same operations.

Throws `InvalidOutputStage` (source `settings.source`) as `operationRoutes`
does, and when `docs.path` is taken by a `get` route.

### diffSchemas

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { diffSchemas } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The changes from `lock` to `current` (both made by `schemaLockOf`), each
classed as `automatic` (afora handles it: an optional key added, a key
removed, a constraint loosened, metadata), `declared` (it needs a `fill`,
a `renamedFrom`, `previousNames` or an `upgrade` step to a version above
the lock's; `satisfied` says whether the code has it) or `check` (a new
unique key: the stored rows must be checked first). `destructive` marks
what deletes stored data once applied: a removed key, the rows of a
previous name, a removed entity. Nested blueprints and records are
compared key by key. Ordered by entity name, then key.

### httpOptionsIssue

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { httpOptionsIssue } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

Why the {@link HttpOptions} are not valid, naming them `where.<option>`;
`undefined` when they are. Other keys of `options` are not looked at.

### operationRoutes

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { operationRoutes } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The route of every operation, by id: `POST {basePath}/{kebab(command)}/{kebab(operation)}`
with `200`, changed by the route the use case declares (`operation.route`)
and, over it, per operation id with `route` and `responses`. Throws
`InvalidOutputStage` (with `source`) when `route`, `responses` or
`security.operations` name an unknown operation, a path parameter is not a
scalar key of the input, or two operations share a method and path. The
routing of the `openapi` sink and of the sinks that serve HTTP.

### outputValueOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { outputValueOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The JSON a sink sends: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))`. Every record
goes through its `toJSON`, so sensitive values are always masked.

### problemOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { problemOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

An RFC 9457 problem for `error`. `issues` (`path`, `code`, `message`; no
values or causes) is present only for a 400, `trace` only with `debug`,
and the `detail` of a 5xx is `"Internal error."` unless `debug` is set, so
internal messages do not leak.

### requestIdHeaderOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { requestIdHeaderOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The header that carries the request id with these options (`"x-request-id"`
for `requestId: true`), or `undefined` without `requestId`.

### routeOptionsIssue

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { routeOptionsIssue } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

Why the {@link RouteOptions} (`basePath`, `route`, `responses`,
`requestId`, `security`) are not valid, naming them `where.<option>`;
`undefined` when they are. Other keys of `options` are not looked at.

### schemaLockOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { schemaLockOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The lock of the entities of `description` (`app.describe()`): per entity,
its schema version, previous names, unique keys and fields (each with its
JSON Schema, whether it is optional or unique, its `fill` and
`renamedFrom`, and the fields of a nested blueprint or record), with
registered properties, blueprints and records resolved and every key
sorted, so equivalent applications give equal locks. The identity keys
and the keys of record plugins are left out.

### schemaLockProblemsOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { schemaLockProblemsOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

Why the code cannot run over the stores `lock` describes: an entity of
the lock that no entity is named, or lists in its `previousNames`, or an
entity whose `schemaVersion` is lower than the lock's. Empty when it can.

### sinkOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { sinkOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

A factory of sink stages: `openapi({ info })`. A sink that needs what JSON
cannot hold (middlewares, an authenticator) takes it as a second argument,
its `hooks`, which `build` receives and the description of the stage
leaves out.

### stageCatalogOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { stageCatalogOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

A catalog of stage `factories`, by name: what resolves the name and
options of a JSON pipe back to a stage. Throws `InvalidOutputStage` for a
function that is not a factory or for two with the same name.

### stageKindOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { stageKindOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

Whether a factory made by `transformOf` or `sinkOf` builds transforms or
sinks, without calling it; `undefined` for any other function.

### statusOf

*function* · tier: adapters · `import { statusOf } from "@afora/core/adapters"`

The HTTP-style status of an error, in this order: `statuses` by exception
name; 400 for invalid input or context (and any exception whose
`details.issues` is a list, except `InvalidCommandEnvironment`, a 500); 404 for a missing entity or operation; 409 for
a unique violation, a concurrency conflict or an entity that already exists; 401 for
`UseCaseInvalidCredentials` and `Unauthenticated`; 403 for `Forbidden`; 422 for a class in `operation.errors`; 500 for the
rest, errors that are not exceptions included. Exceptions match by name,
or by class for `operation.errors`.

## @afora/core/experimental

Tier: experimental (may change in any release). 28 exports.

### DescribedJwtOptions

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { DescribedJwtOptions } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The options of `jwtOf` where they are described (`describe()`,
`afora.json`): the secret is named by its environment variable.

### InvalidJwtOptions

*const* · tier: experimental · `import { InvalidJwtOptions } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

`jwtOf` got options it cannot use, or its secret is missing; `details.reason` says what.

### Jwt

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { Jwt } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Signs and verifies the tokens of one secret (see `jwtOf`).

### JwtAlgorithm

*type* · tier: experimental · `import type { JwtAlgorithm } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The algorithms `jwtOf` signs and verifies with: HMAC with a shared secret.

### JwtOptions

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { JwtOptions } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The options of `jwtOf`. JSON, so they can live in the options of a sink.

### JwtSubject

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { JwtSubject } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

What a token is signed for.

### JwtTokenOptions

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { JwtTokenOptions } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

What changes for one token.

### PropertyLineage

*type* · tier: experimental · `import type { PropertyLineage } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

How a property class came from another one, or from a factory.

### SliceMask

*type* · tier: experimental · `import type { SliceMask } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The keys of `Properties` a slice keeps: `true` keeps a field whole, a nested
mask keeps only its keys, e.g. `{ name: true, address: { city: true } }`.

### SlicedBlueprint

*type* · tier: experimental · `import type { SlicedBlueprint } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The blueprint of `Properties` that keeps only the keys of `Mask`.

### SlicedValue

*type* · tier: experimental · `import type { SlicedValue } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

`Value` with only the keys of `Mask`, in objects, records (by `toJSON`, with
the keys their blueprint requires) and lists.

### StdTokenOptions

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { StdTokenOptions } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The tokens `login` and `refresh` issue: the options of `jwtOf`, plus what
a token says of the entity. JSON, so it lives in an `afora.json`: the
secret is named by its environment variable (`{ env: "JWT_SECRET" }`).
Experimental: it may change in any release.

### UseCaseOriginInfo

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { UseCaseOriginInfo } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Where a use case class made by a plugin comes from, as `useCaseOriginOf` gives it.

### ValueMask

*interface* · tier: experimental · `import type { ValueMask } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

A mask for values, which have no blueprint to check its keys against.

### eventPolicyCatalogOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { eventPolicyCatalogOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

A catalog of event policy factories, by name: what resolves
`{ "policy": name, "options": {...} }` back to a policy. Throws
`InvalidEventPolicy` for a function that is not a factory made by
`eventPolicyOf` or for two with the same name.

### eventPolicyDescriptionOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { eventPolicyDescriptionOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The name and options of a policy made by `eventPolicyOf`; `undefined` for
any other value, such as a handler written by hand.

### jwtOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { jwtOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Signs and verifies JSON Web Tokens with a shared secret (HMAC), on Web
Crypto, so it runs on Bun, Node and Workers alike:

```ts
const jwt = jwtOf({ secret: { env: "JWT_SECRET" }, issuer: "blog" });
const token = await jwt.sign({ subject: user.id, scopes: ["posts:write"] });
const principal = await jwt.verify(token); // { subject, scopes, claims? }
hono(options, { authenticator: jwt.authenticator() });
```

A token is refused (`Unauthenticated`) when it is malformed, signed with
another algorithm or secret, expired, not yet valid, of another issuer,
audience or use, or has no subject. Throws `InvalidJwtOptions` for options
it cannot use, and when the secret of `{ env }` is missing or shorter than
32 characters, on the first token.

### matchesQuery

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { matchesQuery } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Whether `data` is a row of `query`: alive unless `withDeleted`, not expired
by `expiry` (the key of `context.expiry`) unless `withExpired`, and matching
`where`.

### prepareQuery

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { prepareQuery } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Validates query structure and optionally normalizes domain values for storage.

### propertyLineageOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { propertyLineageOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

How `Property` was made: `Base.with(options)`, `optionalOf(Base)` or a
factory (`enumOf`, which registers itself with `recordPropertyLineage`);
`undefined` for a root property, declared with `propertyOf`, which its
`type.name` identifies (`"email"` for `Email`).

### providerDescriptionOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { providerDescriptionOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Describes a named provider; an anonymous one needs an explicit import on extraction.

### sameValue

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { sameValue } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

Structural JSON/data equality without depending on object key insertion order.

### selectRows

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { selectRows } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The rows of `query` after ordering, `after`, offset and limit.

### sliceOf

*const* · tier: experimental · `import { sliceOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

A new blueprint with only the fields of `blueprint` that `selector` names,
recursively into nested blueprints, records and lists (whose wrappers,
optionality and flags are kept). `selector` is a mask, as
`{ name: true, address: { city: true } }`, or a blueprint or record class,
whose keys, at any depth, are the mask. A key `blueprint` does not have
throws `UndeclaredBlueprintProperty`, and is a type error for a mask.

### sliceValue

*const* · tier: experimental · `import { sliceValue } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

`value` with only the keys `selector` names, recursively through objects and
lists, without validating it. A record instance is read by its `toJSON`, so
what is sensitive stays masked; a plain object is copied as it is. A key
missing from `value` is left out. `selector` is a mask or a blueprint or
record class, as for `sliceOf`.

### stageDescriptionOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { stageDescriptionOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

What a stage is: its kind, name and JSON options when it came from a
factory, `{ kind: "opaque" }` otherwise (a hand-written stage needs an
import mapping to be extracted).

### useCaseOriginOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { useCaseOriginOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

The plugin, the repository and the options a use case class was made
from, by a plugin's `make`; `undefined` for a class declared by hand. A
class extending one keeps its origin.

### useCaseTargetOf

*function* · tier: experimental · `import { useCaseTargetOf } from "@afora/core/experimental"`

What a use case plugin reads of `repository`: its entity, its actions and
a plan of every key, to derive blueprints and steps from. `source` names
who asks, in the `UseCaseUnavailable` it throws. Throws a `TypeError` when
`repository` was not made by `repositoryOf`.

## @afora/core/testing

Tier: testing. 7 exports.

### ContractRunner

*interface* · tier: testing · `import type { ContractRunner } from "@afora/core/testing"`

The parts of a test runner the kit uses; `bun:test`, vitest and jest fit.

### HttpProviderContractSettings

*interface* · tier: testing · `import type { HttpProviderContractSettings } from "@afora/core/testing"`

What the kit needs of a sink that serves HTTP.

### MemoryPublisher

*interface* · tier: testing · `import type { MemoryPublisher } from "@afora/core/testing"`

A publisher that keeps what it is given, for tests.

### ProviderContractOptions

*interface* · tier: testing · `import type { ProviderContractOptions } from "@afora/core/testing"`

What {@link providerContract} takes: which optional groups of cases to run,
each defaulting to what the provider advertises in `capabilities`, except the
schema evolution ones.

### httpProviderContract

*function* · tier: testing · `import { httpProviderContract } from "@afora/core/testing"`

The cases every sink that serves HTTP must pass, whatever its server: the
routes use cases declare, where each input key is read from, the context,
access, statuses, problems, cookies, the request id and the document. A
sink built on `compileRoutes` passes when it routes each method and path
to `handle` and sends the result as is.

```ts
import { describe, expect, it } from "bun:test";
import { httpProviderContract } from "@afora/core/testing";

httpProviderContract(
	"hono",
	{ sink: (options, hooks) => hono(options, hooks), fetch: (app, request) => app.fetch(request) },
	{ describe, it, expect },
);
```

### memoryPublisher

*function* · tier: testing · `import { memoryPublisher } from "@afora/core/testing"`

A publisher for `applicationOf({ publishers })` in tests: it keeps each
`{ topic, event }` it is given in `published`.

### providerContract

*function* · tier: testing · `import { providerContract } from "@afora/core/testing"`

Registers the behavior every `IRepositoryProvider` v2 must have. Pass the
`describe`, `it` and `expect` of your runner and a factory of fresh, empty
providers (called once per case).
